notes_for_us: No genre in the index is a two-team pursuit game. Role Sim gave the city and the task stations, Shooter gave the opposed bases, and neither expresses the thing that makes this game what it is — that one side is hiding and the other is hunting across a shared persistent world. The classification is a stitch, not a fit.

A 3,000-word design document produced the same four questions a one-line prompt does, and three of them are about things the document actually specifies. The question cap is sized for thin prompts; on a document this thick the useful question is 'which of the twenty named places must be enterable', and asking it once about four candidates barely dents it.

The prison is the clearest miss: it is named as a map zone, it has geometry, it holds players against their will, and the closest option is building-interior, which says nothing about being unable to leave. A holding area with a controlled perimeter is a real recurring layout concept with no row.

Scale is where this prompt breaks. The skill's own rule says detail wins, which would put a whole city at Block — obviously wrong. I applied the overriding rule about extent and detail not both fitting, but the two rules are stated in different sections and give opposite answers on the same prompt.

notes_for_us: Avoiding the unwanted P6 came down to picking obstacle-jump over path-track. Both describe the same jumping route; one routes P6 and one does not. The genre note tells you the game should stay P0 but the mechanism for achieving that is an undocumented choice between two near-identical option rows, and 'never override a P6' would forbid fixing it after the fact.

The prompt gives a hard 'reach the summit' and the vertical framing rule says one top-down cannot hold a tall climb. That is a real conflict on a very common Roblox game shape, and the only tool for it is a note plus an offer to decompose — there is no route code for 'tall thing, build in vertical slices'.

The lava is the whole theme and the build cannot tell whether it kills you. hazard-kill was left out rather than invented, which is correct by the rules and leaves the map's most obvious feature unspecified.

Five worlds, four gamepasses, five pet rarities: this prompt is mostly a feature list, and mechanics absorbed fourteen entries cleanly. Step 0's third pile is doing the heavy lifting on prompts like this and it worked.

notes_for_us: This is the batch's clean case: six stated features, five of them landed on rows, verdict complete. Worth noting against the long design documents, which all came back partial.

The preset immediately contradicted the prompt. Battlegrounds carries hazard-kill because ring-outs are the Roblox battlegrounds format, and the prompt says flat and rings the arena with buildings. Keeping it per the brief means the image model is being told to cut a pit into a map described as flat — the preset_rejected field records it, but a downstream reader that ignores coverage will build the pit.

Nothing expresses the edge of an arena. The prompt frames the space with tall buildings and a treeline, which is the most common way any bounded arena is closed off, and it had to ship as two free-text entries. boundary-edge exists but only in no-genre, so a genre prompt cannot reach it through the ordered search unless the catalogue is opened, and the catalogue does not list it at all.
